title: Television chain letters
lede: The broadcast ads, a recording from the hotline and a later documentary. These are collectors’ uploads; the 1994 dates are the uploaders’ and match the period the drink was on sale. Upload dates are from the YouTube pages.[^22]

videos.title: OK Soda broadcast ads
videos.caption: A two-and-a-half-minute reel of television spots, titled “OK Soda Broadcast Ads, 1994” by the uploader and posted in June 2014.[^22] The Believer describes the format: a voice reading a chain letter as typewriter text scrolls over a black background.[^13]

videos.title: The hotline: “Thanks for being a devoted caller”
videos.caption: A short recording that the uploader presents as audio from the 1-800-I-FEEL-OK line, posted in September 2014. The year is our attribution from the period the line operated; we could not confirm when the recording was made.[^22][^8]

videos.title: A single 30-second spot
videos.caption: Titled “1994 OK Soda Commercial” by the uploader and posted in May 2022. The date is the uploader’s.[^22]

videos.title: “OK Soda Commercials! All Of Them (I Think)”
videos.caption: A five-minute compilation posted in September 2013 by Fizzled Out, a blog about discontinued sodas. The uploader’s own title admits it may not be complete.[^22][^18]

videos.title: Slate’s Decoder Ring: “The Gen X Soda That Was Just ‘OK’”
videos.caption: A 43-minute episode of Slate’s Decoder Ring podcast about the brand, posted on Slate’s channel in February 2024.[^22] A later retelling, not a period source; nothing on this page is cited to it.
